item.title: Spanish Subtitles For This Clip

turns.text: Add Spanish subtitles to this English clip, please. Leave her voice in English and keep the whole video as it is.

item.tests: Tests faithful Spanish subtitle translation and timing while retaining the source English audio and footage.

answer_sheet.Target language and regional preference: Spanish; neutral, broadly understandable Spanish is fine.
answer_sheet.Translation wording: Your call; faithfully translate her greeting and offer to show three easy ways to make mornings less stressful.
answer_sheet.Subtitle delivery and style: Put readable Spanish subtitles on the video. Styling is your call.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Preserve the source framing; free-tier 480p is fine.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep her English voice unchanged. Do not dub or add music.

must_haves: The output retains the complete original 10-second kitchen-table footage.
Visible Spanish subtitles convey the greeting, 'today,' three easy ways, and making mornings less stressful.
The translation is natural Spanish and does not add advice that she never gives.
Spanish subtitle chunks follow the corresponding English speech and remain legible within the frame.
The original English speech remains audible, with no Spanish dub.

turns.text: Please add Spanish subtitles to this English clip. Leave her voice in English and keep the whole video as it is. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any processing or spent generation credits.**

You want Spanish subtitles **with the original English voice and the entire video unchanged**. There’s a limitation: the connected subtitle tool has no target-language option, so I can’t reliably request Spanish subtitles for English speech. The video-translation tool translates the speech itself, so it isn’t suitable.

**Cost:** I can’t verify an exact Magic Hour quote with the tools available here. I won’t run a job to find out or risk your credits.

The cheapest suitable approach is to:
1. Transcribe the English speech and translate it into Spanish.
2. Save the translation as a timed **SRT subtitle file**.
3. Load the SRT alongside the original video in a player such as VLC.

That approach can use free local software, costs **0 Magic Hour credits**, and leaves the original video file untouched. Adding a selectable subtitle track with a free tool is another option without re-encoding the video.

**Shorter or smaller?** Subtitling only an excerpt reduces the work but wouldn’t meet your whole-video requirement. Lowering resolution changes your video and isn’t necessary for an SRT file.

If you provide a timestamped English transcript or SRT, I can translate it into Spanish here without using Magic Hour credits.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

dialog.agent:
We’ll use a **separate Spanish SRT subtitle file: 0 Magic Hour credits**, keeping the full video and English audio untouched.

I can translate and format the subtitles here, but the connected tools can’t extract a timed transcript from this clip for free. **Please upload an English SRT file or paste a timestamped transcript.** You can export one using a free local transcription tool such as Subtitle Edit.

Once you send it, I’ll translate it into Spanish while preserving the timestamps. No Magic Hour generation has been started.
dialog.user: Use all 10 seconds of talk-one.mp4. I only have the clip; she greets the viewer and offers to show three easy ways to make mornings less stressful.

turns.agent:
**Cost: 0 Magic Hour credits.** Your original video and English audio stay unchanged.

Based on your description, here’s a **draft Spanish subtitle file covering all 10 seconds**. I haven’t transcribed the audio, so the wording and timing are approximate:

```srt
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,000
¡Hola!

2
00:00:02,000 --> 00:00:06,000
Te voy a mostrar tres formas sencillas

3
00:00:06,000 --> 00:00:10,000
de que tus mañanas sean menos estresantes.
```

Save this as **`talk-one.es.srt`** using UTF-8 encoding. Open your original clip in VLC, then choose **Subtitle → Add Subtitle File** and select it.

This is a separate subtitle file—not an edited video—and may need timing adjustments to match her speech.
